title: Austin Street & Finance Decisions 1908
summary:
• **Street Project Stalled**: Council rejected the paving committee's bid for West 5th Street work, with the contractor's certified check returned. The project will proceed at a later date.

• **Financial Oversight**: The Finance Committee approved crediting the city assessor and collector nearly $7,000 in delinquent taxes for 1904, and the city attorney was instructed to pursue lawsuits against property owners owing taxes from 1906-1907.

• **Mayor Vetoes Employee Pay Raise**: Mayor Maddox blocked a $30 ordinance to pay sanitary department workers extra compensation, citing budget constraints and charter rules against mid-employment wage increases. Council failed to override the veto.

• **City Infrastructure**: Council approved $130.50 for a water system at City Hall and authorized a temporary bridge keeper salary, plus requested the Water & Light Commission install an arc light at Sixth and Congress Avenue.

• **Legal Action Against Gas Company**: Council directed the city attorney to sue the Austin Gas Company for allegedly using property (pipes and equipment) that belonged to a defunct water gas company and now belonged to the city.

The Chairman laid before the Council the following veto message of the Mayor .
Austin,Texas,July 18,1908 .
Mayor's veto . Hon City CouncilAustin,Texas . Gentlemen: I respectfully beg to return
disapproved ,your ordinance appropriating the sum of $ 30,00 for the purpose of paying for
extra street work done by the Sanitary Department .My reasons are as follows : First: The
budgeted amount for sanitary work for the year 1908 carries only a sufficient sum for the
monthly payment of the regular employees .
Second: The employees to whom it is proposed to pay this extra allowance,are regular
employees and their compensation was fixed by your body before they received their
appointment,as is required by section 120,City Charter.
Third: Section 69,page 31.,City Charter,expressly prohibits the increase of the
compensation of the City's agents,during the time which they are employed.
Section 122,page 52,makes it unlawful to appropriate out of the general fund so as to
reduce the general fund below the amount estimated in budget ..
The condition of the general fund is now such that we must use the greatest econ-omy,or we
cannot meet our budget.

I,therefore,for the reasons above given must disapprove of your ordinance .
F M Maddox,Mayor .

. Alderman Scott offered the following resolution which was read and adopted.
Whereas serious damage and great inconvenience is caused to boatmen by the obstruction of
piles and other timbers now in the Colorado River just west of the I & G N Ry Bridge, and,
whereas said piles and obstructions were placed in the bed of the Colorado River by the
International and Great Northern Railway Company, or its Contractors in the building of
the new bridge at that point.
Therefore be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin, Texas: That the City
Attorney, and the Street Committee are hereby authorized and directed to communicate with
the proper representatives of the said International and Great Northern Railway Co and
urgently request that all said dangerous obstructions be removed at as early a day as
possible. City attorney to

Gas Company
Alderman Haynes offered the following resolution which was read and adopted; Whereas it
has come to the knowledge of the City Council of the City of Austin that the Austin Gas
Company, a corporation of the City of Austin, is now and has for a number of years been
using personal property belonging to the City of Austin and which was formerly owned by a
defunct Gas Company, known as the "Water Gas Company " and which said Gas Company had
franchise rights, pipes, etc. in the City of Austin, and which said last named company has
defaulted in the payment of taxes to the City of Austin and has permitted their property
to be sold to the City of Austin.
Now, therefore, be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin, that the City
Attorney of the City of Austin be and he is hereby instructed to investigate and at once
file suit against said Austin Gas Company for the conversion, use and application of the
personal property of the said "Water Gas Company" owned by the City of Austin.
